summary: Reflex's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994. A rave-flavoured sample demo that opens with an old-school digi intro before moving into design-led parts.
why: Sceners call it a groundbreaking style change and a milestone in C64 demo design. Demozoo notes it as the 4th best demo in Design #1 (February 1997).

quote.text: Tons of exciting effects. This one really entertained me. Cool techno tunes as well. I particularly like the balls on grid and the pinball physics.

summary: Punkfloyd's realtime demo for the NEC PC Engine SuperGrafx, which took second place in the Realtime Demo compo at Demodays 2012. Code and music are by nop, graphics by LaTortue.
why: A compo podium finish for a SuperGrafx demo. The source code is available if you want to see how it was done.

summary: Impossiblator 3 is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, with code, graphics and music all by Viznut. It came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007, with one person behind every part of it.

summary: HEOHdemo is Shiru's NES demo, which won the Console Demo/Intro compo at CAFe 2019. It carries an epilepsy warning.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2020. Both the source and a writeup are available, so it's a good one to watch and then read up on.

summary: Jitter is a demo for the Atari Lynx by Desire, which won the Atari Lynx Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. Heaven and Axis wrote the code, with a team of graphics artists and music by Nainain and Jakub Husak.
why: A compo winner on the Atari Lynx, with a large team of graphics artists and two musicians behind it.

summary: Detroyt is a ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft that won the Demo compo at ASCii 2003. Code is by psndcj, music by Key-Jee, and graphics by Diver, prof4d and G.D.
why: A compo winner with a clear split between code, music and a three-strong graphics team.

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo with a pirate theme, which came 5th in the Demo compo at X 2016. Nominated in the That's Not Possible On This Platform category at The Meteoriks 2017.
why: Many commenters call it their favourite from X 2016 and think it deserved to place higher. They single out the code, the soundtrack and the run of parts, from Donkey Kong rasters to the endless bobs.

quote.text: Killer music and very fast flow, tons of cool parts.

summary: Backtro is an Amstrad CPC demo from Logon System, released in 2001, with code credited to Overflow.
why: A short factual card is all the fact sheet supports: a single-coder CPC demo from the early 2000s.

summary: Phosphorizer is a 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Loonies and Logicoma. It won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A compo-winning 4K for the Plus/4. Blueberry coded it, H0ffman made the music and Ferris wrote the cruncher.

summary: Dizzzruptor is a multi-part ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Hooy-Program that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2012. Yerzmyey's AY music runs through every part.
why: Six parts from a crew of coders, with guests including Mat, Tygrys and Alone Coder. It won its compo.

summary: Extend's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Zoo 1998. Barfly and Tape coded it, TBB wrote the music and Electric drew the graphics, including interlaced fullscreen pictures.
why: Commenters single out the interlaced graphics, the trancey TBB tune and the sharp, clean-cut way the screens follow one another. One of Electric's pictures is his Zoo 97 graphics compo winner, My Trans.

quote.text: No fuzz about fades and transitions, just sharp cutting. And of course not to forget some of the finest interlace graphics.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s Ghost In The Machine is a demo for the Commodore 64 DTV. It won the Combined Demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2007.
why: Commenters treat it as a proper multipart demo for the DTV and a sign the platform can carry one, picking out the fast shadebobs, the multicolour plasma and Linus's music.

quote.text: Finally a decent multipart demo on the DTV. Great work guys!

summary: Invasion Of The Big Pixels is an MSX demo by Noice, with code by Shadow, music and graphics by Ham and further graphics by ptoing. It took second place in the Combined Demo compo at Grep White 2008.
why: A podium finish for a small MSX team in a combined compo.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Compusphere 2015. Shadow coded it, Redcrab drew the graphics and Stinsen made the music.
why: Commenters like its bug theme, the cute sprites and above all the dot twister plotter, and keep saying they wish it ran longer.

quote.text: Never seen a twister plotter before. Looks great. The SID tune rocks as well with this.

summary: The Asskicker is an Atari 8-bit demo by Shadows that won the Demo compo at QuaST 1996. Konop coded it, Cedyń did the music and Titus the graphics, with a hidden part by Bewesoft.
why: A 128K compo winner whose tags list Gouraud shading, plasma, a zoomer and a Wolfenstein effect. The video is titled AssKicker on steroids, from the Silly Venture 2017 wild compo.

summary: Bonzai's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Gubbdata 2021. It was named Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022.
why: Commenters praise its style, the transitions locked to the soundtrack, and the humour, including the team avatar scroller and a double DYPP. Several say it sets a new bar for C64 demos.

quote.text: Beautiful artwork, music, flow, impressive effects and the Bonzai humour... this one has it all!

summary: Genesis Project's three-disk-side C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2020. Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement and Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2021; source is available.
why: Commenters describe an art-driven demo with a coherent theme, a rich soundtrack and some serious code behind it, notably a full-width bitmap upscroller that streams from disk.

quote.text: It's clearly a labor of love with much attention to detail.

summary: RGBA is a 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, with music by 505 and a font by Ooz. It won the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A compo-winning 16K intro, with a video title that spells the name out as Rasters Girls Beer Atari.

summary: Somewhat Less Limited Capabilities is a ZX81 demo by Noice, which came 6th in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.
why: A ZX81 demo that made the top six in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.

summary: Bauknecht's C64 demo, coded by Mad with music by Mad and Sire and graphics by Sire. It came second in the Wild / Alternative Platform compo at Evoke 2007 and was nominated for a Scene.org Award.
why: Commenters call it fresh and un-C64-like, and rave about its scrollers. Parts are advanced with the space bar rather than running as a trackmo.

quote.text: The rotating scroller is the best oldschool effect I've seen in a long time.

summary: Byterapers Inc.'s C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Assembly 1995. Mr. Sex coded it, Zardax made the music and Mike drew the graphics.
why: Commenters call it a newschool classic and single out Mike's logos and the way the music fits the effects. Demozoo lists it as the joint 6th best demo in Design #1 (February 1997).

quote.text: very nice 4x4 routines, the gouraud at the end is lowreso but fast on the other hand, overall a very well done newschool classic.

summary: The Best Intro Ever is a 4K intro for the C64 by Razor 1911, which won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2016. rez did the code and graphics, with music and the player by 4mat.
why: Commenters single out 4mat's tune, a full soundtrack squeezed into a 4K, and the smooth expanding circles and dots.

quote.text: The tune is awesome, having a full featured soundtrack of this quality in 4K intro is rare.

summary: Timmy is a ZX Spectrum demo by Speccy.pl made for the Timex Computer 2048 and 2068. It won the Demo compo at Riverwash 2014.
why: A compo winner aimed at the Timex Computer 2048 and 2068. Tygrys wrote the code, Ziutek the music, and Piesiu and At0m the graphics.

summary: Reliable Fraud is a ZX Spectrum 48K demo with AY music, made by Zoo. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2011.
why: A compo winner on the plain 48K Spectrum with an AY soundtrack by V0yager. Tygrys coded it and Slayer did the graphics.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 tribute to Star Wars, which won the C64 Demo compo at X 2018. Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2019.
why: Commenters rate the SID arrangements of the film's music above all, along with the humour, the colour-cycling parts and the full-screen pixel art. Some tire of the theme but admit the effort.

quote.text: At first I thought that the Star Wars theme might have worn off a bit recently, but there's so much freshness in this prod it amazes me. The music remixes alone are out of this world.

summary: Scrollwars is a three-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, placing second in the C64 Demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Pål Syversen drew the graphics.
why: Sceners praise the design, the music and Pål Syversen's graphics, plus effects such as the circular twister and twisting torus. Demozoo notes a review in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: Fantastic graphics, Pål you just outdid yourself - it's massive! Code is very fresh, music superb.

summary: 20 Y is a Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with music by Nordloef. The video title dates it 1989 to 2009, and it is tagged as an anniversary demo that loops endlessly.
why: A one-coder Game Boy demo marking an anniversary. It is tagged NSFW, so watch with that in mind.

summary: Shade is a Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Wilds that won the Demo compo at Árok 2007. Larry coded it, Randy made the music and Chronos drew the graphics.
why: A compo winner on the C16/Plus 4.

summary: A joint C64 demo from Fairlight, Censor and Offence that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. Pantaloon and Bob lead the code, with LMan's tune in the end part.
why: Commenters like the pacing and momentum, the colour-cycling spheres and Bob's ball effects, and keep asking how it was done.

quote.text: it has all been put together with so much talent and dedication, and with amazing pacing and forward momentum.

summary: Gnork is a VIC-20 demo by Desire that took third place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. It needs the 16K RAM expansion.
why: A podium finish for a VIC-20 demo at a major party. Heaven wrote the code, BokanoiD drew the graphics and Triace composed the music.

summary: Manifesto is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2014. drwho and Lovebeam share the code and Nick Roll made the music.
why: A compo win in a combined 8-bit field, beating demos from other machines.

summary: Fossil's two-disk-side C64 concept demo that came 5th in the C64 Demo compo at X 2018. Bjørn Røstøen and Knut M. Clausen share the code, Archmage did the graphics and Linus the music.
why: Commenters rate its transitions, sync and soundtrack very highly, and several think it deserved to place above fifth. They also single out Archmage's graphics and the sense of storytelling.

quote.text: I love the music in this one and the whole thing is so smooth.

summary: Irreality 1k is a ZX Spectrum 1K intro by SerzhSoft that won the ZX Spectrum 1k Intro compo at Forever 2014.
why: A compo-winning intro that fits into 1K on the Spectrum.

summary: Quantum Disco Brothers is a 64K intro for the NES by wAMMA. It came second in the Demo compo at Stream 2006.
why: A podium finish for an NES production, built by a team of two coders, an Ilmarque soundtrack and five graphics artists.

summary: The Revision 2012 Invitation is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo from Hooy-Program and Royal Belgian Beer Squadron. Gasman wrote the code and music and FRaNKy the text. It won the Other Platform Demo compo at Datastorm 2012.
why: A party invitation that won a compo in its own right.

summary: BB is a 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K with AY by introspec. It won the 8 Bit 256b intro compo at Multimatograf 2014 and is tagged politics and Russia theme.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte class, tagged with a political theme.

summary: Rain is a ZX Spectrum demo by Life On Mars that took second place in the 8Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2016. It runs on the 48K and 128K models.
why: introspec did the code, graphics and text, working with Diver on design and graphics, and Mister Beep wrote the music.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo that came second in the C64 Demo compo at The Party 1997. Graham coded it, DeeKay drew the graphics and Fanta wrote the music. It is interactive, with controllable effects.
why: Commenters are amazed at how much fits in about 50 KB, from controllable Gouraud shading and 3D dots to a playable engine in the final part, and rate Fanta's tune among the best.

quote.text: I still can't believe how all these effects can fit into 50 KB! ABSOLUTELY AMAZING, especially the playable DOOM clone at the end of the demo.

summary: Over Relaxed is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by sibCrew that won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2017. It is tagged as using ZX multicolour mode.
why: A compo winner with a team of two coders, two musicians and a graphics artist: rook, wbcbz7, Robat, Quiet and Nik-O.

summary: Bonzai and Pretzel Logic's four-disk-side C64 demo that came second in the Demo compo at X 2023. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2024 and for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023.
why: Commenters rate it as a new benchmark for storytelling on the C64, with a mood that shifts from 80s nostalgia to the present, and many call it their favourite of the compo.

quote.text: It is the most rewatchable demo I know, like a favorite movie that you can watch over and over again.

summary: Datafresh is a C64 4K intro by Loonies and Darklite that won the C64 4k intro compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer. Blueberry wrote the code and Response the music.
why: Commenters call it one of the best 4Ks and say it beat bigger demos at the party. They single out the zooming plasma and fast ECM shaders.

quote.text: the code is very very clever here, one of the best 4ks I guess

summary: Some Nasty Effects is a BBC Micro demo by CRTC (shown on a BBC Master) that won the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2015. Puppeh and Joey wrote the code, GreaseMonkey the music and Tunk the teletext final screen.
why: A compo win for a BBC Micro demo, ending on a teletext final screen.

summary: Imation is a TI-8x (Z80) calculator demo by Deus Ex Machina, listed as a 64k, that won the oldskool demo compo at Dreamhack 2000.
why: A compo winner on a TI-8x calculator.

summary: Riyadh is an MSX demo by Bandwagon that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001. nf coded it, Gspot made the music and Scythe and Nitro made the 3D graphics.
why: An Assembly compo winner on MSX, with a credits list that gives 3D its own line.

summary: Hardcore Petting is a silent Commodore PET demo made in PETSCII, coded by Shadow. It took third place in the Oldschool Demo compo at @Party 2010.
why: A podium finish for a demo with no sound at all, built from the PET's character set.

summary: Elements is an Atari Lynx demo by Desire that came 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2017. Heaven coded it, Triace composed the music and Premium and BokanoiD did the graphics.
why: A Lynx demo that made the top five at a major party.

summary: Raiding Party is a Vectrex demo by Rift that took second place in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2017. Fell coded it and Bex made the music.
why: A podium finish for a Vectrex production.

summary: Oric Tech is an Oric demo by Defence Force that took second place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2015. Dbug did the code and graphics.
why: A podium finish for an Oric demo, with an intro tune by Jochen Hippel and sample loops from Kraftwerk's Musique Non Stop.

summary: Evil Influences is a BBC Master demo by Bitshifters and Desire that won the Old School Demo compo at Nova Online 2020. VectorEyes and Henley coded it, Dya made the music and Visionvortex and Luther the graphics.
why: A compo winner and a joint effort between two groups on the BBC Master.

summary: Twistex is a 256-byte intro for the Vectrex by Orb, coded by Ultra.
why: A 256-byte production on the Vectrex.
